Title: hetpaleis leest voor (hetpaleis reads aloud)
Description:
Every first Sunday of the month, we make sure hetpaleis is extra cosy.

Six well-known and lesser-known artists read aloud from their favourite children’s book. This is followed by a (craft) workshop based on the story that’s just been read.

PS: coming and going is no problem, and you don’t have to sit still either.

Title: Wat Macy weet (What Macy knows)
Description:
it could have gone like this he was handsome and clever and funny and she was clever and funny and handsome and they saw each other and thought hey that one and they chatted and laughed and thought funny and handsome and clever and then yes this is what I don’t know when it started and what happened next when the thaw began when everything started to crack

Macy knows a lot. She knows the names of the oceans, she knows the seasons, she knows the names of birds. But as for what happened between her father and mother, she can only guess. So Macy makes up her own version.

Wat Macy weet is about what mothers and fathers say when they no longer know themselves, stories to fill the void, being someone else week after week and the importance of knowing where you stand.

Femke Heijens ( HUGS ) directs Hélène Devos in a monologue about a sensitive daughter of divorced parents. Angelo Tijssens (co-screenwriter of, among others, Close ) is behind the script, loosely based on Henry James’s What Maisie Knew (1897), a novel about a girl who, following her parents’ divorce, lives alternately with her father and mother while trying to take control of her own life. She takes on their roles and tries to understand the world through play.

Title: the beach
Description:
‘With your back in the sand and the sun on your face. Your beautiful best friend helps you to rub sunscreen on your body. Her hands move up and down. She smiles. You’re dying to tell her how wonderful she looks today. And how much you love her. But you’re afraid of ruining your friendship.’ // ‘Are people becoming more and more prudish about sex? Is there more polarization? Are things different in other countries? Here, gay sex is forbidden because we believe it’s against nature.’ // ‘No towel, no swimwear – can't be bothered. If you’re as confident as I am, you always have to be able to improvise. You always have to be ready to land a punch and take a hit. I’m with the bruzz, hunting for the huzz.’ // ‘That it’s not just something mysterious. Dialogue sex. Ruleless sex. Crazy sex. Wild sex.’ // ‘I want to find love without having to make love.’

Together with eleven young people, you experience a day and a night on the beach. The murmur of the waves forms the soundtrack to their thoughts on sexuality – so many desires, questions, beliefs, doubts, fantasies. Their inner, personal reflections on intimacy and eroticism become as visible as their hot skin.

‘Until my unattainable, huge, octopoid desire disappears into the depths of the dark ocean, looking for its next victim.’

The text of the beach was created over a period of five months by ten young people from Antwerp on the basis of writing sessions, improvisations, conversations and interviews.

Title: HUGS
Description:
He likes to sit on his sofa. She has her dog. How do you become friends? With strange moves and crooked turns. The beat sets them in motion. Will they find each other?

To the beats of Hannes d'Hoine, Femke Heijens and Marieke Dilles create a wordless world. HUGS is a playful, visual performance about loneliness, (in)tolerance and friendship.

With few words, lots of music, movement and visual language, two strangers experience the ups and downs of forming a new friendship. At first glance, the two characters have little in common, but they nevertheless engage in a game of attraction and repulsion. Their rapprochement is awkward, moving and recognisable—for both children and adults.

Making friends is not always easy. Sometimes it is awkward, sometimes we make mistakes. HUGS reminds us that this is perfectly normal—and often very funny.

The rhythmic beats of Hannes d'Hoine bring the performance to life and create an energy that carries the characters and the children along. Because little spoken language is used, HUGS is accessible to everyone, regardless of age or background. Perfect for young children who are learning social skills.

Using a fat suit as a costume is a deliberate artistic choice. The fat suit allows the actor to transform their appearance. It creates a new body, a different character.

Title: PIEDESTAL
Description:
In PIEDESTAL , seven Pulcinellas take centre stage: the first without arms, the second without eyes, the third without legs, the fourth without a voice, the fifth without a nose, the sixth without ears and the seventh without a heart. Together they try to build a structure, but their respective limitations constantly get in the way, bringing the project to a standstill. Eventually, the Pulcinella without a heart decides to take a leap and climb towards the elusive ideal. At first, no one dares to follow her, until the least acrobatic one of the group, driven by sheer willpower, ascends without hesitation.

PIEDESTAL explores the tension between ambition and acceptance, a quest for the balance between limitation and infinite possibilities – an enchanting and inclusive performance at the intersection of theatre and circus.

Title: I love (and hate) you, Belgium
Description:
Actor and theatre-maker Armin Mola has travelled to various corners of our country in recent years with his hit show I love (and hate) you, Iran . Along the way, thanks to his many encounters and conversations, Armin gathered a wealth of information about local culture.

In I love (and hate) you, Belgium , he sketches out in a humorous and critical way what, for him, makes Belgium Belgium. Armin slips into the skin of a range of characters with different world views and experiences. Freestyling with voice, language and accents, he weaves his personal story with social and political questions around nationality and identity.

I love (and hate) you, Belgium has room for the anger, the cold, the obstacles and the rain, but also for the great love for language, its accents, juiciness and tongue-twisters. Armed with nothing but words, Armin Mola wins over the whole country.

Title: Claudette
Description:
Claudette is turning 90. And that calls for a celebration. Or does it? Claudette is tired of being alone for days on end, of eating soup every day and always sitting on the sofa. She longs to feel alive again. Fortunately, she can count on her grandson who, juggling on roller skates, brings meaning back into her life.

Claudette is a delightful tribute to wrinkles filled with wisdom and experience. An ode to a whole generation of grandmothers and an ode to intergenerational bonds.

This original street theatre performance is both poetic and funny. It has won many international awards (including Best Show Award – Umore Azoka 2024 and Best Performance Award – TAC de Valladolid 2024) and has been touring the world for the past three years.
